Photograph: Elizabeth Cook/PA Frances Mao Mon 9 Nov 2026 10.19 EST First published on Mon 9 Nov 2026 04.36 EST Share From 1h ago 09.26 EST Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault offences
 Judge Bennathan asks Brand to stand up as he passes his sentence judgment.
 He says the sentence for rape is nine years imprisonment.
 The total sentence is 10 years, six months, with the sexual assault offences.
 The judge gave prison sentences of nine months, 18 months, and eight months for those three offences.
 Prosecutors had called for the judge to mete out a sentence of this severity, for a category one penalty which ranges from 10-15 years.

 8m ago 10.19 EST Police: 'Russell Brand has been held accountable for his crimes'
 The lead detective on the case, Det Supt Andy Furphy, has just spoken outside the courtroom saying today’s sentence is a significant milestone, one that “means Russell Brand has been held accountable for his crimes.”
 He goes on to praise the six women who bravely came forward and endured court interrogation to get to where we are today.
 “I hope they recognise just how powerful their actions have been and the difference they may make to others,” says Furphy.
 Full comments below:
 double quotation mark My thoughts today are with the women who came forward and made this investigation possible.
 Reporting sexual offences can be incredibly difficult and they have shown immense bravery, dignity, and resilience throughout what has been a lengthy and challenging trial process.
 The victims have had to revisit deeply traumatic experiences and endure significant public and media attention.
 I hope today’s outcome provides some measure of closure, and allows them to continue rebuilding their lives.
 Their courage in coming forward has not only led to this outcome, but may also give confidence to others who have suffered sexual violence, to seek help and report what happened to them.
 I hope they recognise just how powerful their actions have been and the difference they may make to others.
 From the very beginning, our investigation was never about Russell Brand’s profile, status, or celebrity. Our focus has always been on the women who reported these offences, and on conducting a thorough and impartial investigation into the allegations that they made.
 Share Updated at  10.19 EST 16m ago 10.11 EST Judge added two years to rape sentence for Brand removing condom and other serious aggravating factors
 Regarding the rape sentencing, Judge Bennathan noted that Brand ordering the then 21-year-old woman to “clean your sheets” was “an additional… humiliation”.
 He also said that Brand removing the condom without her consent, and ejaculating into her “which led to months of fearing she might have HIV” were “serious further aggravating factors”.
 He said those actions “must raise” his sentence punishment by two years above the starting point.
 As I reported earlier, the judge reduced the sentence by one year for mitigating factors such as Brand not having any serious prior convictions.
 Share 25m ago 10.02 EST These are the details of the rape conviction, where Brand in 2009 anally raped a 21-year-old fan of his, removed the condom and ejaculated in her, humiliated her afterwards and left her terrified that she might have contracted HIV.
 The judge summarised the crime as following:
 double quotation mark She was a huge fan of yours, which you were happy to exploit. She had willing consensual sexual activity with you after your show. You took her phone number and if anyone still needs any demonstration of your contempt for your casual sexual partners, you stored her number under “T” for “tart”.
 You invited her to your house a few days later. There you put on a condom at her request and had vaginal sex, to which she consented.
 You then flipped her over, removed the condom and, without asking, forced your penis into her anus, causing her great pain. She asked you to stop, then asked you again loudly. You replied, and I quote, “I want you to feel my cum”.
 You ejaculated. She was distraught and in severe pain. The bed was heavily soiled by blood, sperm and faeces. You told her it was her mess, and made her try to clear it up. Shortly after, you went off to get ready then went to work. She was driven to a nearby underground station by your driver who for some reason had tissues ready, to hand to her as she wept. She was left distraught, in pain and terrified she might have contracted HIV.
 Judge Bennathan noted how Brand’s actions had caused “significant and long-lasting” harm to the woman.
 double quotation mark In her victim impact statement she wrote of struggling to eat and sleep, of taking two to three months off from work and of abandoning the career she had embarked upon.
 Although the rape was 17 years ago, she still finds it affects her ability to form new friendships and to know when she can trust people. From her evidence at trial I also know she developed an alcohol problem, partly as a result of your attack on her.
 Share Updated at  10.04 EST 32m ago 09.54 EST Russell Brand was sentenced to nine years for the rape conviction alone. 
 He was acquitted of two other rape counts, but because of this count, has received such a serious sentence behind bars.
 Judge Bennathan went into length on this offence, and I will get into that in the next post.
 Share Updated at  09.54 EST 38m ago 09.49 EST The judge had said he was “very conscious” that Brand’s imprisonment would “deprive your children of the presence of their father”.
 double quotation mark That sad loss to them, however, is caused by your serious offending.
 Brand’s lawyer Ian Winter KC earlier had strenuously made the case that a lengthy sentence would have a “catastrophic” impact on Brand’s wife and three children.
 Brand was taken into custody immediately after a jury found him guilty last Thursday so has not had the opportunity to say goodbye in person to his family.
 Share 42m ago 09.45 EST Judge Bennathan also commended the Met Police for “their hard work in gathering evidence and taking great care of all the women who testified.”
 As I reported earlier, one of the victims said she had wanted to withdraw her case after the stress and pressure and public attention, but she persisted with the support of specialist police teams.
 The Met Police have said they expect other women may come forward to report their experiences of abuse and assault.
 Share 45m ago 09.41 EST Judge paid tribute to 'determination and bravery' of women who came forward
 Right before delivering his sentence decision, Judge Bennathan said:
 double quotation mark Finally, before passing sentence, I pause to pay tribute to the determination and bravery of all the woman whose evidence I have been recounting.
 I do not increase your punishment becauseof it but all those women had to face being confronted and being told they lied, or twisted the truth, and or they’d agreed to your sexual demands. That was all done because of you, and your instructions.
 Share 48m ago 09.38 EST Officers have taken Brand out of the courtroom.
 He has served a few days at HMP Wandsworth already, after being denied bail last Thursday following his conviction.
 Share 55m ago 09.31 EST Brand must serve two-thirds of the 10-and-a-half years sentence before he will be eligible for parole, says the judge.
 That means he will be behind bars for seven years.
 Share Updated at  09.34 EST 1h ago 09.26 EST Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault offences
 Judge Bennathan asks Brand to stand up as he passes his sentence judgment.
 He says the sentence for rape is nine years imprisonment.
 The total sentence is 10 years, six months, with the sexual assault offences.
 The judge gave prison sentences of nine months, 18 months, and eight months for those three offences.
 Prosecutors had called for the judge to mete out a sentence of this severity, for a category one penalty which ranges from 10-15 years.
 Share Updated at  09.42 EST 1h ago 09.24 EST The judge says with the mitigating factors in play, he will reduce his sentence for Brand by a year.
 He has not given the full sentence yet.
 Share 1h ago 09.23 EST Judge Bennathan has repeatedly called Brand a sexual predator during his address so far.
 He notes mitigating factors of no crimes having been reported in the past 17 years, and some evidence testifying to Brand’s character.
 Share 1h ago 09.20 EST 'You thought fame meant you could act however you liked'
 The judge, laying out the crimes, notes Brand’s “staggering arrogance” and how his entourage regularly indulged Brand’s actions.
 Three of the four crimes took place in public settings, in front of other people – at a bar, radio station and a setting where an advert was being filmed. Others in the room laughed after the assaults, the women said.
 double quotation mark These insults in front of an audience, said after the assault amount to an additional humiliation.
 double quotation mark The whole episode reeks of casual disrespect, and your belief that fame meant you could act however you liked, when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live.
 Share Updated at  09.24 EST 1h ago 09.16 EST The judge is relaying the sexual assaults Brand committed against the women.
 He starts with the attacks on one woman in a pub in London where Brand groped the breast of a fellow party attendee.
 “The effect on her had her wandering the streets of London, phoning a friend in the middle of the night, tearful and distressed.”
 He outlines another assault, where Brand, visiting a radio station with an entourage launched himself at a woman, groping and kissing her in front of her colleagues and his entourage.
 He notes the attack’s impact on her, how it damaged relationships with her male colleagues.
 “There was the added humiliation of you assaulting her in front of an audience and the laughter afterwards”.
 View image in fullscreen Mr Justice Bennathan passing sentencing at Southwark crown court Photograph: Cameras in Court/PA Share Updated at  09.25 EST 1h ago 09.08 EST Judge Bennathan starts with Brand’s climb to fame 20 years ago.
 “About 20 years ago, Russell Brand , you were becoming famous. You were clever – and in many people’s eyes, funny and charismatic.
 “You had also become a sexual predator,” he says.
 “Your status protected you until 2023 when journalists published allegations” about his rapes and sexual abuse of women.
 Such public reporting “empowered” other women to come forward to police, says Bennathan.
 Share Updated at  09.10 EST 1h ago 09.04 EST Judge Bennathan is about to begin his sentencing remarks, having considered the submissions from the prosecutor and Brand’s defence lawyer this morning.
 A reminder that Russell Brand, once one of Britain’s most high-profile actor-comedians, was convicted last Thursday of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. 
 A jury of eight men and four women found him guilty of attacking four of six women on allegations dating back to 2004 . He was cleared of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.
